info.title: GreenCalculus API
info.description:
Sourced greenhouse-gas emission factors and audit-traced carbon calculations. Every value returns with its exact source reference and data version — reproducible and citable. Free key at https://greencalculus.com/developers/.

SCOPE: this document describes every endpoint we publish a callable example for — the data, calculation, discovery and watch endpoints. It deliberately excludes the control plane behind greencalculus.com (billing, sign-in, key management, admin), which is not a customer contract and is free to change, and /v1/account/webhook, whose configuration is session-only by design and therefore cannot be exercised with the bearer token this document describes. Those exclusions are enumerated and enforced by scripts/check-openapi-drift.mjs, so an endpoint is absent here because it was excluded, never because it was forgotten.

get.summary: Resolve one factor by canonical key (value + full provenance)

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Serve this factor as it stood at an ARCHIVED data version. On a hit you get the archived row, served_version is the version you asked for, and version_pin reports matched: true, reproducible: true. Two misses, and they behave differently. (1) The version is NOT in the archive: 200 carrying the CURRENT row, with version_pin.matched: false naming as_of_requested and listing every archived version available — unlike POST /v1/calculate/*?as_of=, which 400s instead. So read version_pin before treating a response as pinned; do not infer it from the status code. (2) The version IS archived but holds no row for this key — it did not exist yet, or was withdrawn at or before it: 404 not_found, naming the key and the version, and saying whether the key is in the CURRENT corpus so a real absence is distinguishable from a mistyped key. GET /v1/factors/{key}/history lists every version that recorded it. Case (2) returned 200 with the current value in a browse envelope until 2026-09-10; it now refuses, because serving a current value under a past version label is the one answer this endpoint must never give.

200.description: Factor with value, source id, source reference, data version

404.description: Unknown key, or a key with no row at the requested ?as_of= version

get.summary: Version history — what this factor has been
get.description: Every version the reproducibility archive holds for one key, with the value each version served and whether it was a change or a withdrawal. Derived from the same per-key archive index and the same read that answers ?as_of=, so it cannot disagree with the archive. Requires a key (any tier). History begins at the delta watershed; a short list means a stable factor, and the payload says so.

404.description: Key unknown to both the corpus and the archive

get.summary: Browse/search the corpus (open — no key, values included)

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text. Every whitespace-separated word must appear in the row name or canonical key (dots/underscores/hyphens read as separators, so a pasted canonical key finds its own row). Results are relevance-ranked.

parameters.name: key_prefix
parameters.description: Anchors at the START of the dotted key — "electricity" matches nothing; use search for words appearing anywhere.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Taxonomy family slug (hyphenated). An unknown value returns 200 with an empty result and the valid families listed in meta.warnings.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: base64(canonical_key) from meta.next_cursor. Preferred over offset — stable across data-version bumps, and required for paging relevance-ordered search results.

200.description: Matching factor keys, names, sections. meta.warnings explains any filter that matched nothing.

400.description: gc_unknown_param — a query parameter this endpoint does not accept. The message names the offender and lists the accepted set. Other 400s: gc_limit_too_large, gc_offset_invalid, gc_cursor_invalid, gc_section_conflict.

post.summary: Activity → emissions (activity × factor, with unit conversion + working + scope)

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Run this calculation against an ARCHIVED data version. Every factor used is the row as it stood at that version, and meta.gc_version, meta.version_pin, the citation and the receipt all report it. Unlike GET /v1/factors/{key}?as_of=, an unavailable version is REFUSED (400) rather than served from current data with a label: a calculation returns a single figure that goes into a report under a receipt, so it must be the version it claims. A factor key that did not exist yet at that version is refused for the same reason. Archived versions are listed in the error, and by GET /v1/factors/{key}?as_of= on a miss.

country.description: Optional. The country the ACTIVITY belongs to — ISO3, ISO2 or a name ("deu", "DE", "Germany"). When given, the response carries factor.resolution stating whether the factor used is published for that country (tier: exact), is a global figure applied to it (global), or belongs to a different country (proxy, with proxy_of naming which). Omit it and no geography claim is made — the response is unchanged. A country we do not recognise yields no claim rather than a wrong one.

post.description: Version pinning is NOT available on this engine: the pin resolves keys named `*factor_key`, and this endpoint is addressed by `material_key` (and its per-module rows). Sending ?as_of= here is a 400 rather than a silent fall back to current data — a calculation that carries a receipt has to be the version it claims.

country.description: Optional. The country the ACTIVITY belongs to — ISO3, ISO2 or a name ("deu", "DE", "Germany"). 200.description: Per-stage embodied carbon + boundary total; module D separate; data gaps flagged

post.summary: PCAF Part A financed emissions (attribution + audit trail)
post.description: Version pinning is NOT available on this engine: the pin resolves keys named `*factor_key`, and this endpoint is addressed by `sector_key`, or by caller-supplied emissions with no factor at all. Sending ?as_of= here is a 400 rather than a silent fall back to current data — a calculation that carries a receipt has to be the version it claims.

holdings.description: Each holding may carry its own optional `country`, overriding the request-level one — a portfolio routinely spans economies, and the spend-based intensity used for one borrower may come from a different country than the next.

post.summary: Freight (GLEC) — the factor's denominator picks the method: mass × distance (tonne-km) or TEU × distance (TEU-km)
post.description: Send `mass` for a factor denominated per tonne-km, `teu` for one denominated per TEU-km (the sea-container family — a TEU is a twenty-foot container slot, not a mass). Sending the wrong one is refused with 422 `gc_freight_basis_mismatch` rather than silently multiplied.

422.description: Unknown factor, or the activity input does not match the factor's denominator

items.description: Each item is dispatched to the same handler as its standalone endpoint, so an item may carry its own optional `country` and gets the same factor.resolution back. There is no batch-level country — items in one batch routinely belong to different countries.

503.description: Shared calculation capacity full — a deliberate global concurrency cap protecting the origin, not an outage. Honour Retry-After. Identical repeat calls are served from a deterministic cache and never consume capacity.

post.summary: Resolve — plain-text description → ranked factor keys + confidence

description.description: Plain-language description of the factor you need.

section.description: Optional. Restrict candidates to one MB section.

limit.description: Optional. Number of ranked candidates to return.

200.description: Ranked candidate factor keys with confidence scores. Each match carries country_iso3 and geo_match ("exact" | "global" | "proxy"); a "proxy" match is a factor from a different country than the one asked for, and its confidence is discounted accordingly.

get.summary: Status — current health and measured uptime
get.description: Open (no key). Current operational state, uptime over 24h/7d/30d, and a log of healthy/degraded transitions. Measured by a probe running every ~5 minutes against the edge factor store, the WordPress origin and a real calculation round-trip. The probe runs INSIDE this Worker and therefore cannot observe the Worker being entirely down — the response says so rather than implying total coverage.

get.summary: Change feed — what each data release changed
get.description: Open (no key). Data releases newest first, each with added/changed/withdrawn counts and a link to its per-release record. Derived at publish time from the same delta the reproducibility archive stores, so this feed cannot disagree with ?as_of= about a release. Records begin at the delta watershed (meta.record_begins); earlier versions remain archived and pinnable but are not summarised.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A version from a previous page's next_cursor; resumes after it. Must be at or after meta.record_begins — an earlier version is archived and pinnable but was never summarised, so it cannot be resumed from.

400.description: Unknown parameter, bad limit, or unknown cursor — named in the error

get.summary: One release — every row it added, changed or withdrew
get.description: Open (no key). The full entry list for one data release. Each entry is checkable at verify.greencalculus.com/{key}@{version} without an account. A version older than the record (or never published) is a 404 that says which releases are recorded.

404.description: No change record for that version — the error names the recorded range

get.description: Open (no key). Also served at /openapi.json. Point a generator, Postman or your editor at it.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 description of this API

get.summary: The sourcing queue — factor gaps the telemetry actually recorded
get.description: Open (no key). Rebuilt daily from 90 days of misses, never hand-edited. A key appears only after crossing meta.floor requests, which is what separates demand from one-off probes; naming misses the API recovered with suggestions are excluded as discovery bugs rather than data gaps. An empty list is a statement about the record, not about demand, and meta.note says which.

get.summary: The factor keys this account is alerted on

200.description: The current watchlist and its cap

post.description: A release that touches the key emails old to new with the versioned verify link. A key that is not in the corpus is REFUSED with 422 rather than accepted as an alert that could never fire.

422.description: The key is not in the corpus, so watching it would never alert

post.description: POST rather than DELETE: credentialed CORS on this API allows GET and POST only.

get.summary: What changed for your watched keys between two dates
get.description: The reporting-period question, answered directly: per key, the value at each boundary, whether it moved, the versions that touched it, and a proof link per side — the evidence a restatement decision needs. A `from` older than the change record clamps to the archive watershed and the response says so.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Defaults to today.

200.description: Per-key boundary values and proof links

post.description: Off by default. Each edition covers exactly the period since the last one — anchored to itself, so it fits any financial year with no configuration. Quiet periods still send: "your saved figures stand" is the answer a reporting team needs.

400.description: cadence must be off, monthly or quarterly

get.summary: Coverage — which countries we hold data for, and how much
get.description: Open (no key). Per country: how many of 13 inventory families we hold, the row count in each, and a band (complete / partial / minimal). Answer "do you cover my country?" before integrating. Derived from the live corpus at request time, so it cannot drift from the data. Measures PRESENCE, not sufficiency — a country showing fuel:7 has seven fuel rows, which may not answer a given question; the response repeats this in a caveat field. Returns counts only, never factor values.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: One or more ISO-3166 alpha-3 codes, comma-separated.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Only countries holding data in this family.

parameters.name: min_score
parameters.description: Only countries covering at least this many of the 13 families.

200.description: Coverage matrix + meta (families, bands, filters) + caveat

400.description: Unknown parameter or unknown family — named in the error

post.summary: Check — which published factor is each of your numbers, and is it still right?
post.description: Open (no key), up to 25 rows per request, limited per IP. Send the factors your inventory already uses, each as a description, the value AS TYPED (a string keeps its precision: "0.207" matches anything that rounds to it) and the unit as written. Each row comes back with the published factor it matches (source, edition, line), a status (current, outdated, fix, review, unverifiable, notcomparable), findings such as an old edition, old IPCC warming values, a 1,000x unit slip, net instead of gross calorific value or an upstream (WTT) factor used for combustion, and the current value to use instead. UK government factors carry every edition 2019-2026 except 2021; other sources are current-edition only, so a non-UK value can be identified but not yet called out of date. Nothing is substituted, and the request body is neither logged nor stored.

example.description: Optional. Marks a request as a demonstration (our own page sends it for its worked example) so it is not counted as a check.

value.description: As typed. Send a string to keep trailing zeros.

unit.description: As written, e.g. kgCO2e/kWh, kg CO2e per litre, kgCO2e/pkm, GWP.

200.description: One verdict per row, a status summary, the index the check ran against and its coverage

400.description: Body is not JSON, rows is empty, or more than 25 rows

429.description: Too many checks from this address; Retry-After says when to try again

get.summary: Absence — why a factor is NOT in the corpus
get.description: Open (no key). The reasoned counterpart to /v1/coverage: where that reports a zero, this reports why. Each record carries the subject, the publisher we checked, the route we tried, a confidence and a review date. Five classifications: "structural" (no publisher issues this anywhere — stop retrying), "not_yet_sourced" (a publisher exists and is named; our backlog), "refused" (we found it and declined; the reason is stated), "held_not_counted" (we DO hold it — see we_hold for the key — and the coverage metric cannot see it), and "coupled" (zero only because another family is zero). These are authored judgements about what the world publishes, not values derived from our corpus, so each carries a review date and reports stale:true once past it.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO-3166 alpha-3 code.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Inventory family, as used by /v1/coverage.

parameters.name: classification
parameters.description: structural | not_yet_sourced | refused | held_not_counted | coupled.

200.description: Absence records + the classification legend + caveat

400.description: Unknown classification — the valid set is named in the error

get.summary: Source feed — one publisher's dataset, whole
get.description: Open (no key). Every row we hold from one public-domain publisher, with that publisher's licence, issuing body and retrieval date, and the exact source reference behind each value. Feeds exist for a NAMED SET of sources, not for every source id in the corpus — a source we have not cleared for republication has no feed, and asks for one are refused rather than quietly answered from somewhere else. The id is case-insensitive. Everything else in the corpus is readable through GET /v1/factors, which carries the same values, provenance and licence per row.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Source id, case-insensitive. Currently DEFRA_2026, DEFRA_2025, EMBER_YEARLY_ELECTRICITY_2025.

200.description: The publisher record plus every factor transcribed from it

404.description: No feed for that source id. The error names the ids that do have one.

get.summary: Full consolidated factor feed (Business plan and above)

Error.description: The single error envelope, on every non-2xx response from every endpoint. Stated on /developers/docs and enforced at the gateway for origin-raised errors too — read the code from error.code.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Transport-level: unauthorized, forbidden_tier, not_found, rate_limited, quota_exceeded, overage_cap_reached, busy, origin_unavailable, invalid_request. Validation codes are namespaced gc_* and named per endpoint (gc_unknown_param, gc_limit_too_large, gc_offset_invalid, gc_cursor_invalid, gc_section_conflict, and the per-engine gc_<engine>_* set).

message.description: Human-readable and specific — a 4xx names the offending parameter and lists the accepted set.
message.example: Unknown query parameter: bogus. This endpoint accepts: offset, cursor, limit, section, key_prefix, family, search. Free-text lookup is ?search=.

details.description: Present only when the failing endpoint attached structured detail beyond the HTTP status.

Receipt.description: Deterministic tamper-evidence. To verify: remove the `receipt` and `attribution` keys from the response, sort every object's keys recursively, serialise to JSON with slashes and Unicode unescaped, and SHA-256 the result — it equals `receipt.id` with the `gcr_` prefix stripped. The receipt's own `verify` field states the same recipe.

verify.description: Plain-language instructions for recomputing the digest.

Uncertainty.description: The publisher's own stated range, never derived by us. null means NOT RECORDED — explicitly not a claim that no uncertainty exists.

Citation.description: A ready-to-paste citation assembled from the source registry.

FactorCitation.description: The canonical citation for one factor row, built by the API (src/citation.ts) and printed VERBATIM by every official client (Sheets add-in, JS and Python SDKs, MCP). Format: "<factor name>. <source name> — <publisher>, cell <cell_ref>, retrieved <date>. via GreenCalculus data version <version>, factor <key>. <proof URL>". On GET /v1/factors/{key} the version is the one actually SERVED, so a ?as_of= lookup cites the pin. Present on rows from 2026-09-09. The format is a published specification, free for anyone to implement against their own data: https://greencalculus.com/developers/citation/

text.example: UK grid electricity — location-based (generation). UK Government GHG Conversion Factors 2026 — Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), cell 'UK electricity'!E25, retrieved 2026-06-18. via GreenCalculus data version 2026.186, factor grid.gbr.electricity.location_based. https://verify.greencalculus.com/grid.gbr.electricity.location_based@2026.186

SourceRef.description: Provenance to the line. Carried on 100% of rows — where in the source document the value was read, not just which document. A workbook cell where the publisher ships a workbook (DEFRA); otherwise the table, annex clause or page they did ship (IPCC, CBAM, ECCC).

FactorRow.description: One corpus row as returned by browse/search. Carries the full row INCLUDING factor.value — the browse endpoint is open and unmetered by design, because our data is overwhelmingly open-licensed at source and gating it would make this API worse than the original publisher. What a paid plan adds is the right to REDISTRIBUTE, not the ability to read. (Note: the MCP search_factors tool DOES project rows down to key/name/section — that projection is deliberate and specific to that tool.)

gwp_set_basis.description: How we know the GWP set — "published" where the source states it, "inferred" where we deduced it. null means not recorded, which is deliberately NOT the same as published.

uncertainty_basis.description: "none_published" means the publisher states plainly that no range exists. null means not recorded — a different fact from silence.

components.description: Per-gas decomposition keyed by gas (co2, ch4, n2o…), each with its own cell_ref. Lets a consumer re-base AR5↔AR6 without us.

note.description: Includes what the publisher did NOT provide, stated verbatim.

licence.description: The licence this row is published under, and whether the Business redistribution grant covers it. Present on the open browse from MB v2026.181 — the full terms, the required credit and the publisher are listed once per source under meta.licences. Absent (not empty) where no licence is on record: an empty value would read as "no licence applies".

FactorList.description: Browse/search results. Open — no key, no quota. Values ARE returned on this route. Use /v1/factors/{key} when you want one row plus its audit envelope (provenance, licence, verification) or a version pin via ?as_of=.

canonical_total.description: Rows in the whole corpus at this version.

next_cursor.description: base64(canonical_key). Prefer this over offset — stable across data-version bumps, and required to page relevance-ordered search results.

filters.description: The filters as the endpoint understood them — echoed back so a silent mismatch is visible.

warnings.description: Why a filter matched nothing. A 200 with an empty array and a warning is the normal way this endpoint says "no such thing".

licences.description: One record per DISTINCT source on this page, keyed by source id — so the licence detail is carried once rather than repeated on every row. Join via factors[].source.id. `attribution` is present ONLY where the licence grants redistribution and requires a credit; its absence on a non-redistributable row is deliberate.

Provenance.description: Where the number came from and whether you may republish it. Built from the source registry — src/envelope.ts.

issuer.description: The issuing descriptor of this edition (MB `body`), present only when it differs from publisher.

redistributable.description: Whether the Business redistribution grant covers this row. Fails closed — a source whose licence has not been assessed is false, not null.

overrides_source.description: Present only when this row carries a licence its source does not (a publisher republishing third-party data under its own terms, e.g. CBAM Annex II). licence, redistributable and redistributable_basis above are then the ROW's; this block keeps the source's own answer beside them.

since.description: Data version at which the row-level answer was recorded.

source_ref.description: Where the restricting text was read.

Verification.description: What was actually checked — computed at serve time, not asserted.

components_sum_to_value.description: Whether the per-gas components sum to the headline. null where the row carries no components — the absence of a check is not a failed check.

FactorLookup.description: One factor with its value and the full audit envelope. Served from the edge KV store.

factor.description: The full row. Its `citation` is built at served_version, so a pinned lookup cites the pin.

version_pin.description: Present only when ?as_of= was sent — and not even then if the key did not exist at an archived version you asked for, which falls back to the browse envelope instead. `matched: false` means the requested version is not in the archive and the CURRENT value was served — check it before treating a response as pinned.

Attribution.description: The credit the licence requires, or null on a plan that waives it. Was a bare STRING before 2026-08-25; the original string is preserved unchanged at `text`. `html` is a ready-to-paste anchor so that complying is less work than not complying, and `url` points at the public proof page for the exact factor and data version this answer used — your own audit evidence, not a marketing link.

text.description: The plain credit line. Identical to the string this field used to be.

html.description: A single anchor, no classes and no styling, ready to paste.

url.description: Proof page for the factor this answer used, pinned to the data version — e.g. https://verify.greencalculus.com/grid.gbr.electricity.location_based@2026.181. Null where no single factor identifies the answer. The version is deliberate: an unversioned link would silently re-point at whatever the figure becomes.

required.description: Whether this plan must display the credit. Reports the licence position, not a technical control.

ProofUrls.description: Every factor used by this answer, as a public proof URL pinned to the data version. A portfolio calculation may list many; cite per line from here. Contains no request data — each URL is a fact about the GreenCalculus corpus and is identical for every caller.

FactorMiss.description: A key that does not exist. Carries candidate keys rather than a bare 404 — most misses are a naming difference, not a coverage gap. The documented error envelope is present alongside the bespoke fields.

Calculation.description: The SINGLE-FACTOR engines — ghg-activity, freight, spend-based and business-travel. The full working, never just a total. The block echoing your input is named per engine (activity | transport | spend | trip); everything else below is shared. The other four engines answer a different question and have their own schemas: ElectricityCalculation, PcafCalculation, EmbodiedCalculation, BatchCalculation.

range.description: Propagated from the factor's published uncertainty. null where the publisher states none — not a claim of certainty.

activity.description: ghg-activity only. freight sends `transport`, spend-based `spend`, business-travel `trip`.

resolution.description: Present ONLY when the request sent `country`. tier is exact | global | proxy; proxy_of names the country the factor actually belongs to. Absent means no geography claim was made — NOT that the match was exact.

working.description: The arithmetic in the open — unit conversion and the formula as evaluated.

unit_conversion.example: 5 MWh = 5000 kWh (converted to the factor's basis)

formula.example: 5000 kWh × 0.13096 (kg CO2e per kWh) = 654.8 kg CO2e

reproducible.description: How to pin this result for an audit.

ElectricityCalculation.description: GHG Protocol Scope 2 — reports location-based and market-based SIDE BY SIDE, which is why this engine does not share the single-factor shape. market_based is null unless you supply a market instrument.

standard.example: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance — location-based + market-based

market_based.description: null when no market instrument was supplied — the absence of a market figure, not a zero.

PcafCalculation.description: PCAF financed emissions, per holding and in aggregate. The data-quality score is PCAF's 1-5 by DATA SOURCE TYPE — it is a property of YOUR inputs and asset class, not of our factor.

asset_class.description: The single asset class, when every holding shares one; null for a mixed portfolio.

holdings.description: Per holding, so a portfolio total can be traced to the line that produced it.

audit.description: The formula applied, the methodology source, and every factor used.

formula.description: One named formula per step — attribution_factor, financed_emissions, weighted_dq_score — each written out in full.

EmbodiedCalculation.description: Whole-life embodied carbon, EN 15978 modular. Per-material and per-module, with data gaps declared rather than silently zeroed.

has_data_gaps.description: true where a module carries no factor. The gap is declared, never treated as zero.

boundary.description: The EN 15978 modules this figure covers.

stages.description: Per EN 15978 life-cycle stage. `in_boundary` says whether the stage counts toward this result — a stage OUTSIDE the boundary is still reported, with its value, rather than hidden.

BatchCalculation.description: Up to 100 mixed-methodology calculations in one call. A failed item does not fail the batch — it lands in results with its own error.

total.description: The summed emissions across items that succeeded.

results.description: One entry per input item, in order. Each is the engine's own response shape, or an error for that item alone.

Resolve.description: Plain-description → candidate factors, ranked. Deliberately NOT a single answer: every live defect this endpoint produced was a CONFIDENT wrong answer, so each match carries a confidence, a label and the reasons behind it.

country_iso3.description: The country parsed out of the description, or null.

tokens.description: How the description was tokenised — shown so a bad parse is visible rather than mysterious.

geo_match.description: "proxy" is a factor from a DIFFERENT country than the one asked for; its confidence is discounted accordingly.

scope.description: GHG Protocol placement of this row. THIS IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES A RANKED LIST DECIDABLE: "UK grid electricity" returns four exact-country rows spanning 0.11507 to 0.28064, and `ghg_protocol` plus `basis` are what tell them apart — two are scope2 (location-based and residual mix, both wanted for dual reporting) and two are outside_scopes (a lifecycle intensity and a biogenic memo) which must never enter a Scope 2 total.

basis.description: What the publisher measured — the boundary. Distinguishes same-named rows that differ only in method.
basis.example: direct combustion at the generator; generation basis — transmission and distribution losses EXCLUDED

label.description: Set to "review" on low confidence, a thin match, a proxy geography, a demoted row, or an `outside_scopes` row returned ALONGSIDE an in-scope one (a memo figure standing next to the inventory figure it would be mistaken for). A set that is entirely outside_scopes — a product-footprint or CBAM query — is NOT demoted, because there is nothing there to confuse it with. Treat "review" as needing a human: a bare float cannot warn anyone.

why.description: The reasons behind the label, in plain language.

absence.description: Present when nothing matched AND we hold a reasoned absence record explaining why — including the case where we DO hold it under another name.

Coverage.description: Country × family coverage, generated from the live corpus. Scores measure PRESENCE of a family, never sufficiency — a country can score 13/13 and still lack the row you need.

families.description: The thirteen family slugs mapped to their human labels.

bands.description: Counts per band. complete = 10+ of 13 families present, partial = 4–9, minimal = 1–3.

families.description: Row count held per family. 0 means we hold none.

Check.description: Per-row verdicts for factors you already use: which published factor each value is (source, edition, line), whether it is current, and what is wrong with it.

index.description: What was checked against: build date, MasterBrain version, DEFRA editions held.

coverage.description: Plain statement of which sources carry edition history and which are current-only.

match.description: The published factor the value matched: source ids and names, line, unit, value, a link to that edition (edition_link) and, when the match is on the current edition, its proof page (proof_url).

current.description: The current value to use instead, with the percentage change and its proof page (proof_url) where we hold the factor. Suggested, never substituted.

Absence.description: The reasoned counterpart to coverage: what we do NOT hold, and why. A classification tells you whether waiting for us is worth it.

classifications.description: The vocabulary and what each class commits us to — structural, not_yet_sourced, refused, held_not_published, not_surveyed.

covers.description: ISO3 codes this record accounts for.

evidence.description: Public pointer to the gap classification that produced these records.

Status.description: Recorded uptime from a probe inside the API worker. A window reads null until the collected history spans it — we do not extrapolate a short record.

uptime_pct.description: Keyed 24h / 7d / 30d. null means not yet measurable, NOT zero.

uptime_basis.description: When collection started, how many checks, and the date each window becomes reportable.

caveat.description: Includes the probe's own blind spot — it runs inside the worker, so it cannot see the worker being wholly down.

current.description: null when the key is withdrawn from the live corpus.

Roadmap.description: Factor gaps the telemetry actually recorded, most-requested first. Rebuilt daily from 90 days of misses; a key appears only after crossing the request floor in meta.floor, which is what separates demand from one-off probes. An empty list is a statement about the record, not about demand — meta.note says which.

generated.description: ISO timestamp of the last rebuild.

floor.description: Requests a key needs before it is listed.

WatchList.description: The factor keys this account is alerted on when a release touches them.

WatchMutation.description: The watchlist after the change, and which key moved.

WatchDiff.description: What changed for the watched keys between two dates — the value at each boundary, whether it moved, and a proof link per side. Dates resolve to data versions through the change record; a `from` older than the record clamps to the archive watershed and says so.

note.description: Present when there is nothing to diff, or when a boundary was clamped.

Digest.description: The summary cadence for this account. Off by default. Each edition covers exactly the period since the last one, so it fits any financial year without configuration.

OpenApiDocument.description: This document. An OpenAPI 3.1 description of the endpoints listed here.

ChangesList.description: Data releases, newest first. Per-release records begin at the archive's delta watershed (meta.record_begins); earlier versions are archived and pinnable via ?as_of= but not summarised.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as ?cursor= to resume. null on the last page.

ChangesRelease.description: One release: every factor row it added, changed or withdrew, each independently checkable on its verify page.

truncated.description: true when the release changed more rows than one response carries; the KV record is complete.

value.description: The NEW headline value. Absent on withdrawn rows.

SourceFeed.description: One publisher's dataset, whole: every row we transcribed from it, with the publisher, the licence, the retrieval date and the exact source reference per row. The unit of CITATION rather than the unit of query — you take this when you want to hold a publisher's set, not when you want one number.

api_endpoint.description: The origin route this feed is projected from.

dataset.example: UK DEFRA fuel combustion emission factors (2026)

next_update.description: When the publisher next issues, and how long we take to reconcile — stated so a stale figure is predictable rather than a surprise.

sources.description: The publisher record: id, name, issuing body, url, licence, year, retrieval date.

Corpus.description: Bulk feed, Business and above. Redistributable rows ONLY — filtering is driven by a per-source licence tier recorded against the data, and a source whose position has not been assessed is withheld. Every row carries redistributable: true so you can verify what you received.

bearerAuth.description: Your API key, e.g. "Bearer gc_live_…". Get one free at https://greencalculus.com/developers/.
